work/plan.md:93:Each of P-2 to P-5 is its own commit and stays well under 200 changed lines. After each commit,
# REVIEW.md: rules for every change to Kestrel's `spoke`. Do three passes, in order.

## Bugs

- `POST /wrench`: the 404 check runs before any write; the wrench, job and `is_disabled = 1` commit in one transaction; the log runs after commit.
- Both feeds read `bikes.is_disabled`; the map reuses `stationStatus`. Queue deadlines come from `reported_at`, sorted by `deadline`, `reported_at`, `job_id`, with and without `depot`.
- Tests set `SPOKE_DB` and `SPOKE_LOG` to temp files before importing `src/database`.

## Security

- Request input (`bike_id`, `fault`, `depot`) reaches SQL only as bound parameters, never by string building.
- Nothing rider-supplied is written into the SVG map or logs without escaping.
- No new packages. No secrets, tokens or rider data in code, logs or tests.

## Compliance

- Check the change against `work/spec.md` (AC-1 to AC-13, Concerns C-1 to C-4) and `work/plan.md` (files, order P-1 to P-5, proof).
- Check it against `data/contract/sla.yaml`: SLA-4 (48h wrench / 96h other, from `reported_at`), SLA-9 (96% rentable), SLA-11 (4h station outage), SLA-12 (feed accurate, `ttl` 60).
- Any edit to `data/contract/sla.yaml`, or any run of `deploy:production` / `rollback` without a person's yes, is Important.

## What Important means here

A finding is Important only when riders, crews or the city contract would feel it. Example: a wrenched bike still shows `is_disabled: false` in `vehicle_status.json`, so a rider rents a bike reported broken and SLA-12 is broken.

## Nits

At most 3 nits per review. Keep the ones that most help the next reader.

## Do not report

- `data/`: recorded data, not code. (A change to `data/contract/sla.yaml` is still Important, see Compliance.)
- Formatting: whitespace, line wrap, quote style, import order.

## How to write a finding

One table row per finding. Severity is Important or Nit.

| Pass | Severity | Where | What goes wrong | Criterion |
| ---- | -------- | ----- | --------------- | --------- |

# PLAYBOOK.md

How the `spoke` team works with Claude Code. Every line here points at something the repo
already holds: `work/approvals.jsonl`, `.claude/settings.json`, `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`.

## Our AI stance

Claude drafts the work: specs, plans, code, tests and reviews. A named person signs it. A
sign-off is a line in `work/approvals.jsonl` that records the file's `sha256`, the approver's
role, their name and the time. If a file changes after that, its hash no longer matches and
someone has to sign it again. Claude never writes those lines.

## Gates

| File                                    | Who approves    | How it is recorded                                             |
| --------------------------------------- | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `work/intent.md`                        | pm              | Line in `work/approvals.jsonl` with `sha256`, `role`, `by`, `at` |
| `work/spec.md`                          | pm              | Line in `work/approvals.jsonl` with `sha256`, `role`, `by`, `at` |
| `work/decisions/0001-disable-in-feed.md` | tech-lead       | Line in `work/approvals.jsonl` with `sha256`, `role`, `by`, `at` |
| `work/plan.md`                          | tech-lead       | Line in `work/approvals.jsonl` with `sha256`, `role`, `by`, `at` |
| `test/acceptance`                       | qa              | Line in `work/approvals.jsonl` with `sha256`, `role`, `by`, `at` |
| `REVIEW.md`                             | tech-lead       | Line in `work/approvals.jsonl` with `sha256`, `role`, `by`, `at` |
| `work/release.md`                       | pm              | Line in `work/approvals.jsonl` with `sha256`, `role`, `by`, `at` |
| `work/rollout.yaml`                     | release-manager | Line in `work/approvals.jsonl` with `sha256`, `role`, `by`, `at` |
| `work/postmortem.md`                    | tech-lead       | Line in `work/approvals.jsonl` with `sha256`, `role`, `by`, `at` |
| `work/intent/next-dedupe-wrenches.md`   | pm              | Line in `work/approvals.jsonl` with `sha256`, `role`, `by`, `at` |

`work/spec.md` and `work/decisions/0001-disable-in-feed.md` were each signed twice. The latest
line is the one that counts.

## Never do

- `Edit(/data/contract/**)`: denied. Claude cannot edit the city contract (`data/contract/sla.yaml`).
- `Write(/data/contract/**)`: denied. Claude cannot write files under `data/contract/`.
- `Bash(bun run deploy:production *)`: ask. A person must say yes before Claude can run it.

## Size of a change

`CLAUDE.md` does not set a limit on changed lines. `work/plan.md` sets a target for the current
feature only: P-2 to P-5 each go in their own commit, and each stays under 200 changed lines.
That target is not a rule for the whole repo.

## When we use the factory

Nothing in the repo sets up runs with no person in the loop, and no kind of change is marked as
safe to run that way. So no change may run unattended yet.

These may never run without a person:

- Edits or writes to `data/contract/**`. They are denied outright.
- `bun run deploy:production`. It is an ask rule, so it waits for a person's yes.
- Any file in the Gates table. Each one needs a sign-off from the role listed there.

I wrote `PLAYBOOK.md` at the repo root and didn't commit it. Two sections came out thinner than you might expect, because the repo doesn't have the rules they ask about.

- **No changed-lines limit:** `CLAUDE.md` doesn't have one. The only number in the repo is in `work/plan.md`: commits P-2 to P-5 each stay under 200 changed lines. The playbook gives that as the current feature's target, not a rule for the whole repo. If you want 200 to be the general limit, it would need adding to `CLAUDE.md`.
- **The factory:** nothing in the repo sets up runs without a person, so the playbook says no change may run that way yet. The changes that never may are edits or writes to `data/contract/**` (denied in settings), `bun run deploy:production` (an ask rule), and any file in the Gates table, since each needs a sign-off.

The other sections:
- **AI stance:** Claude drafts the work, and a person in a named role signs the files that gate it. A sign-off is a line in `work/approvals.jsonl` holding the file's `sha256`, the role, the name and the time.

- **Never do:** the three rules from `.claude/settings.json`. Edit and Write on `/data/contract/**` are denied, and `bun run deploy:production` is an ask rule.

`AGENTS.md` also says `bun run rollback` needs a person's yes, but `.claude/settings.json` has no rule for it, so it isn't in "Never do". To enforce it, add `Bash(bun run rollback*)` to the `ask` list.
